messages:
jordan-finops: Hey team — noticed a spike in failed Stripe webhook deliveries this morning. Do we have any alerts? A bunch of refunds/invoice.paid events bouncing with 410 signature errors.

sam-eng: saw that too. errors in the connector logs show 'signature verification failed'. the webhook consumer uses the stripe signature header with a tolerance of 300s.

lina-ops: checking host metrics — NTP jitter alert on billing-connector-1 between 03:12-03:45 UTC. clock skew reached ~7 minutes. we had an ntpd restart during a kernel update window.

levi-billing: that's bad. when Stripe sends webhook it includes t= timestamp and v1=signature. if our local time is off, the verification fails. customers impacted: roughly 9 invoices/refunds that day, some triggered DLQ.

stripe-webhook-bot: Delivery failure summary: 9 events failed verification (types: charge.refunded (4), invoice.payment_succeeded (3), invoice.updated (2)). Attempts: 3 per event.

sam-eng: grabbing a sample failure log: 
```
level=error msg="signature verification failed" component=webhook-consumer event=evt_1Kk9 payload_ts=1700000000 local_ts=1700000420 tolerance=300
```
notice local_ts is 420s ahead of payload_ts in this sample.

jordan-finops: some of those failed events included refunds that didn't reach NetSuite; a few customers show unapplied payments in Stripe. We need to reprocess without duplicating downstream posting.

lina-ops: I've corrected the NTP config and restarted chronyd on the fleet. clock skew is back <1s now. I'll keep monitoring.

sam-eng: proposed short-term mitigation: increase Stripe signature tolerance to 900s and mark any incoming event that falls outside original tolerance but inside extended window as 'replay-suspect' so we can do idempotency checks before reapplying. This lets the connector accept slightly skewed events but avoid duplicate application.

levi-billing: ok but we must be careful — relaxing tolerance risks replay attacks. We need to enforce strict idempotency on NetSuite side: always check if event id or stripe_refund_id already processed. Our DLQ processor already checks for processed_refunds, but the webhook consumer bypassed it because verification failed earlier.

jordan-finops: for the 9 failed events can we backfill safely? Which ones are high priority?

levi-billing: priority: refunds first (4) then invoice payments. I'll make a list. Also want automated reconciliation script to find stripe events that landed in failed_verification and map to NetSuite transactions.

sam-eng: I opened a PR to add: 1) temporary tolerance bump flag (feature flag off by default), 2) a 'verification_fallback' path that will attempt to re-fetch the Stripe event via API if verification fails, compare idempotency, and only accept if not processed. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/512

lina-ops: FYI the kernel patch that triggered ntpd restart was rolled back on the nodes that were unhealthy. Ops will add a pre-reboot check to ensure chronyd is stable. Also added an alert rule: if clock_skew > 60s -> paging to ops.

stripe-webhook-bot: Action created: BILL-926 - reprocess failed_signature DLQ and run reconciliation.

jordan-finops: can Levi run the DLQ reprocess for the 9 events once Sam's fallback is in place? We need to ensure the memo/credit flow is correct. Also include an audit note on each NetSuite memo referencing the Stripe event id.

levi-billing: yes. will wait for PR to hit staging. I'll run reprocess in staging first and summarize results here. Also will add a 'source_event' custom field on NetSuite memo to store the stripe event id.

sam-eng: timeline: PR in code review, can merge after a quick security review. plan to deploy the flag to staging in 2 hours, then to prod after smoke tests.

jordan-finops: thanks. long-term we should add a runbook: if clock skew incident happens, don't relax verification without ops sign-off; instead use API re-fetch + idempotency as primary fallback.

lina-ops: agreed. I'll draft runbook and add to infra runbooks. Also will run a 7-day lookback to find any other nodes that showed NTP jitter.

levi-billing: note for accounting: list of impacted customers and suggested actions: for refunds not applied, create customer-level credit memos and tag for month-end adjustment if necessary. for invoice payments that didn't reach NS, we'll post them with the stripe_payment_id and reconcile.

jordan-finops: perfect. keep this thread updated with reprocess results. :thumbsup:
